title: Is it just me or is agentic trade execution suddenly not working with claude in Robinhood?
author: Absolutkush

comments.author: Blotter-fyi
comments.body: I think these models have weird safeguards that don't allow them to place trades automatically. Sucks. Had to build my own tooling to skip past a lot of this stuff. But you're right, it's a problem

replies.author: Absolutkush
replies.body: I was able to successfully execute 3 days ago on the 22nd.

replies.author: Blotter-fyi
replies.body: There's an [app](https://agency.trading/) that solved some of these issues with these LLMs (uses different system prompts so the LLMs are not always declining trades), worth trying.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: Where does the Claude-to-Robinhood flow stop: does Claude refuse to invoke the trading tool, does the tool return an authentication error, or does Robinhood reject the submitted order? The exact error text and which connector you're using would help distinguish those. Before retrying, check Robinhood's order history to see whether an order landed despite a missing confirmation.

replies.author: Absolutkush
replies.body: The agent says its not able to do that, its outside its functions and when I dug in to troubleshoot with the orchestrator it seems to be something from the instructions and safeguards in the session but from anthopics side. Not my instructions.

comments.author: pigeon_shit
comments.body: Check your connector permissions. Mine suddenly changed between yesterday and today.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Robinhood has no official stock order API, so whatever connector this is either drives the website or goes through an unofficial wrapper, and both break the moment Robinhood changes something on their end. That's the part nobody says when they demo agentic execution: the flow is only as stable as a page layout.

Honestly the safeguard people are annoyed about is the one bit I'd keep. The other half of this is the thing I built, Quantradin: an agent writes and tests the strategy and it runs on paper, free, and the broker key on it is read-only, so it can close or cancel but never open a position. Not the same as live execution, but it's the part I'd want working first. It's by name or on my profile if you want a look.
